name: FluxDown
one_liner: Free, ad-free IDM alternative: HTTP, FTP, torrent, eD2K and HLS/DASH on a Rust engine.

text.why: IDM is Windows-only and paid ($24.95 plus renewals, per the README's comparison table); FluxDown offers the same style of dynamic segmentation as AGPL-3.0 open source on Windows, macOS, Linux, Android and NAS (Docker, Synology, QNAP, OpenWrt). Every byte of progress is tracked in SQLite so downloads survive reboots, and Chrome, Edge and Firefox extensions intercept browser downloads. A built-in local MCP server with 12 tools lets AI clients add and manage downloads.
text.take: Download managers are an old genre; combining desktop, Android and NAS with torrents, streaming and MCP in one free app is not.
build: Run the headless server on a NAS with RSS subscriptions as an unattended fetcher, or wire the MCP endpoint so an AI agent queues and monitors downloads for you.

who.situation: the same segmented downloads through a browser extension
a headless Docker/Synology/QNAP server for remote downloads

who.role: Researchers and creators pulling large files
who.situation: HLS/DASH streams and torrents in one queue

start.text: 1. Get a package from GitHub Releases or https://fluxdown.zerx.dev/#download (Windows setup.exe · macOS .dmg · Linux .AppImage/.deb · Android .apk · NAS Docker ghcr.io/zerx-lab/fluxdown-server)
2. Install the browser extension (Chrome Web Store · Edge Add-ons · Firefox Add-ons)
Build from source (Flutter SDK · Rust · Rinf CLI): git clone -b main https://github.com/zerx-lab/FluxDown.git
cd FluxDown && flutter pub get && rinf gen

caveat: AGPL-3.0 licence (modified copies offered over a network must publish source). Windows requires 10 or later (per the website); Linux builds are x64 only; the NAS build is a headless server. No cost, no account. Community channels are GitHub Issues and a QQ group.

license.scope_text: Release source if you redistribute or host it as a service.
